references.title: LMFDB, Elliptic curve 232425.a1 over Q
references.note: Minimal model y^2 + y = x^3 - 525x + 10156; Cremona 232425a1, conductor 232425 = 3^2·5^2·1033, rank 3, trivial torsion; short model y^2 = x^3 - 8400x + 650000. Lists exactly the 42 integral points of this node's conclusion.

references.title: R. J. Stroeker, B. M. M. de Weger, Elliptic binomial diophantine equations, Math. Comp. 68 (1999) 1257–1281
references.note: Solve C(n,4) = C(m,6) by elliptic logarithms; the parent's assembly maps that equation onto this minimal model by x = 15m(m-5)/2 + 25, y = 225n(n-3)/2 + 112. Paper not opened here; attribution as in BBdW 2017's proof of Thm 2.2.

references.title: R. J. Stroeker, N. Tzanakis, Solving elliptic diophantine equations by estimating linear forms in elliptic logarithms, Acta Arith. 67 (1994) 177–196
references.note: The method by which integral points of a rank-r elliptic curve are determined completely (Baker-type lower bound, then LLL reduction); implemented in Sage and Magma.

summary: Known. The integral points of the elliptic curve 232425.a1 (y^2 + y = x^3 - 525x + 10156) are a published computation: the LMFDB lists exactly the 42 in this node's conclusion, found from a Mordell–Weil basis by the elliptic-logarithm method. Not formalised: a Lean proof would need the Mordell–Weil group and a Baker-type bound. This node is the whole number-theoretic content of its parent; the parent's assembly, which maps the binomial equation onto this curve, is proved.
model_and_tooling: Claude Opus 5.5 through Claude Code; LMFDB curve pages read 2026-10-29; point lists re-checked in Python (each point satisfies the equation, and a search over |x| <= 3e6 finds no other)
